items.whyRight: Push and pop share one end; the newest unfinished item is visible.

items.prompt: Validating matching parentheses typically uses a stack to store what?
items.whyRight: Openers push; closers must match the top opener.
whyWrong: Storing everything wastes space without helping matching.
A queue would serve the wrong end.

items.prompt: DFS of a graph/tree implemented iteratively usually models the fringe with a?
items.whyRight: LIFO expands the deepest pending node first.
whyWrong: Edge sets track membership, not expansion order.

items.prompt: Undo in an editor maps cleanly to a stack because?
choices: The last edit is the first one reversed
Edits must be replayed in random order
Undo needs O(n) search by timestamp key
whyWrong: Random order would not be undo.
Keyed search is a different structure.
Command objects often sit on stacks.

items.prompt: Push and pop on an array-backed stack are amortized?
items.whyRight: Most operations touch one end; rare resizes amortize.
whyWrong: Strict linear every time would mean shifting the whole stack each push.
Quadratic is not the stack story.

items.prompt: Monotonic stack problems keep indices of candidates that are?
choices: Still useful because nothing to their right has invalidated them yet
Always sorted by value ascending forever
Stored in a hash map keyed by value
items.whyRight: You pop when a new element breaks the monotonic invariant.
whyWrong: The structure is monotonic while useful, not a permanent global sort container.
Multiple comparisons across the scan are normal.
Maps alone do not maintain the left-to-right candidate order.
